questions.question: The primary goal of digital forensics is to recover lost passwords.
questions.explanation: Digital forensics aims to preserve and analyze digital evidence for investigations.

questions.question: A chain of custody must document every person who handled the evidence and why.
questions.explanation: Yes, chain of custody is a detailed log of all handling events to ensure evidence integrity.

questions.question: Logical acquisition captures unallocated space and deleted file fragments.
questions.explanation: Logical acquisition only copies active files and directories; physical acquisition captures unallocated space.

questions.question: In the forensic lifecycle, the analysis phase focuses on filtering and extracting relevant data.
questions.explanation: Analysis is interpretation and reconstruction; examination handles filtering and extraction.

questions.question: A write-blocker prevents writes to the evidence drive and must be tested before use.
questions.explanation: Write-blockers ensure read-only access; always validate with a non-evidentiary drive.

questions.question: File carving relies on file system metadata to locate deleted files.
questions.explanation: Carving searches for file headers and footers in raw data, independent of metadata.

questions.question: The Master File Table (MFT) is the central metadata structure of the FAT file system.
questions.explanation: MFT is used by NTFS; FAT uses the File Allocation Table.

questions.question: A hash match between a forensic image and the original drive proves the content is identical.
questions.explanation: Matching cryptographic hashes confirm that every bit is the same.
